title: Asperuloside suppressing oxidative stress and inflammation in DSS-induced chronic colitis and RAW 264.7 macrophages via Nrf2/HO-1 and NF-kappaB pathways.
authors: Chen, Yong-Er; Xu, Shi-Jie; Lu, Ying-Yu; Chen, Shu-Xian; Du, Xian-Hua; Hou, Shao-Zhen; Huang, Hai-Yang; Liang, Jian
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Asperuloside通过Nrf2/HO-1和NF-kB通路缓解结肠炎，仅涉及小分子-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), which mainly include Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), are chronic idiopathic inflammatory disease of the gastrointestinal tract for which effective pharmacological treatments are lacking or options are very limited. PURPOSE: Here, we aim to investigate the therapeutic effects of an iridoid glycoside, asperuloside (ASP) on mice experimental chronic colitis induced by dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) and further explore underlying mechanisms in vitro and in vivo. METHODS: LPS-treated RAW 264.7 cells showed inflammation and were assessed for various physiological, morphological and biochemical parameters in the absence or presence of ASP. Chronic colitis was induced by 2% DSS in mice, which were used as an animal model to explore the pharmacodynamics of ASP. We detected p65 and Nrf2 pathway proteins via Western blot and RT-PCR analysis, assessed the cytokines TNF-alpha and IL-6 via ELISA, tested p65 and Nrf2 nuclear translocation via fluorescence. In addition, the docking affinity of ASP and p65 or Nrf2 proteins in the MOE 2015 software. RESULTS: We found that ASP attenuated weight loss, disease activity index (DAI) and colonic pathological damage in colitis mice and restored the expressions of inflammatory cytokines in the colon. In addition, ASP restored antioxidant capacity in DSS-induced chronic colitis mice and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells. Furthermore, ASP suppressed oxidative stress through increasing Nrf2, HO-1 and NQO-1 proteins expressions, and down-regulated nuclear levels of p65 to inhibit DSS-induced colonic oxidative stress and inflammation. Validation of the molecular docking results also indicated that ASP interacts with Nrf2 or p65 proteins. In summary, ASP improved DSS-induced chronic colitis by alleviating inflammation and oxidative stress, activating Nrf2/HO-1 signaling and limiting NF-kappaB signaling pathway, which may be an effective candidate for the treatment of IBD.
abstract_zh: 背景：炎症性肠病（inflammatory bowel diseases, IBDs）主要包括克罗恩病（Crohn's disease, CD）和溃疡性结肠炎（ulcerative colitis, UC），是一种慢性特发性胃肠道炎症性疾病，目前缺乏有效的药物治疗方案或治疗选择非常有限。目的：本研究旨在探讨环烯醚萜苷类化合物车叶草苷（asperuloside, ASP）对葡聚糖硫酸钠（dextran sulfate sodium, DSS）诱导的小鼠实验性慢性结肠炎的治疗效果，并在体外和体内进一步探讨其潜在机制。方法：采用脂多糖（LPS）处理的RAW 264.7细胞诱导炎症，在存在或不存在ASP的情况下评估各种生理、形态和生化参数。通过2% DSS诱导小鼠慢性结肠炎，作为动物模型探讨ASP的药效学。通过Western blot和RT-PCR分析检测p65和Nrf2通路蛋白，通过ELISA评估细胞因子TNF-α和IL-6，通过荧光检测p65和Nrf2核转位。此外，在MOE 2015软件中评估ASP与p65或Nrf2蛋白的对接亲和力。结果：我们发现ASP减轻了结肠炎小鼠的体重下降、疾病活动指数（DAI）和结肠病理损伤，并恢复了结肠中炎症细胞因子的表达。此外，ASP恢复了DSS诱导的慢性结肠炎小鼠和脂多糖（LPS）刺激的RAW 264.7细胞中的抗氧化能力。进一步地，ASP通过增加Nrf2、HO-1和NQO-1蛋白表达来抑制氧化应激，并下调p65的核水平以抑制DSS诱导的结肠氧化应激和炎症。分子对接结果的验证也表明ASP与Nrf2或p65蛋白相互作用。总之，ASP通过减轻炎症和氧化应激、激活Nrf2/HO-1信号通路并限制NF-κB信号通路来改善DSS诱导的慢性结肠炎，可能成为治疗IBD的有效候选药物。
